video_title: What Happens When Humans Get Rabies?

segments.segment_title: What Happens When Humans Get Rabies?
segments.text: This is one of the deadliest viruses on Earth. It silently destroys your brain before you even notice you're infected. And by the time symptoms start to appear, it's too late. Yeah, we're talking about rabies. Every year, nearly 60,000 people are killed by this merciless and unstoppable disease. Today, we'll explore how it ravages your body in each stage of the infection, from first exposure to your transformation into a drooling, raging zombie.

Rabies is transmitted through the saliva of infected animals and enters your body mainly through  open wounds, inflicted in most cases by the animal. It can also enter through previously unhealed wounds. There’s fear that, in some rare cases, you don't even need to be bitten by the rabid creature. About 90% of human rabies cases  are due to dog attacks,  but scientists at the University of Montreal have found evidence of humans getting infected with bat rabies without a single bite or scratch. Since rabies is growing in their brains, animals with the disease will drastically change their behavior. They become more aggressive,  lose control of parts of their body, experience seizures, and, of course, the infamous constant drooling. This is the virus taking over the host’s body and turning them into a puppet that will transmit the disease to a new host by attacking it.

Once you are infected, the virus starts to replicate slowly. So slowly that your body won't notice that it's been invaded. Your immune system thinks everything is fine and makes no effort to combat the virus. This allows the rabies to spread. Sluggishly and unnoticed. This is known as the incubation period and can last from 1 to 3 months after exposure, depending on the part of your body where the infection started. Its only target is to make it to your nervous system. Once it's there, sorry to tell you, but it's over. It will completely melt your brain.

Once it penetrates the spinal cord, it travels to the brain and relentlessly starts reproducing. At this point, your first symptoms will begin to appear. The first ones may be similar to the flu, but soon the real ones  start to show themselves: delirium, hallucinations and hyperactivity. And this is just the beginning.

Once the virus has reproduced in your brain, it moves on to the rest of your body through your nerves in search of its next victim. It infects your salivary glands, causing an excess of infected drool. Swallowing and drinking water will be almost impossible. Rabies wants your mouth to be ready to transmit it. At this stage, rabid animals, including you, will be more aggressive and prone to biting. That’s because you don’t have much time left. After two days of rage, you’ll fall into a coma and die of organ failure. Without receiving the vaccine, rabies is 100% fatal, so if an animal bites you,  notify health authorities  and seek medical help immediately. Remember,  once rabies gets into your nerves,  it’s over. Now, if you want to learn  the best way to survive  this deadly virus, we have the perfect video for you. Just stick around here on How to Survive.
